lab_questions.title: Multi-Warehouse Inventory Allocation & Concurrency
lab_questions.description: An e-commerce fulfillment engine needs to allocate inventory from multiple regional warehouses. The current system fulfills orders naively by checking only the first warehouse, causing artificial stockout rejections or race condition overselling across concurrent checkout requests.
lab_questions.startup_command: python manage.py migrate && python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8010

tasks.title: Split-Warehouse Stock Allocation
tasks.description:
The `POST /api/orders/{id}/fulfill/` endpoint checks only a single warehouse. If an order requires 10 units and Warehouse A has 6 while Warehouse B has 4, the API immediately throws an `OUT_OF_STOCK` error.

**Goal:** Implement multi-warehouse fulfillment allocation. If a single warehouse cannot fulfill the full requested quantity, greedily allocate available stock across the minimum number of warehouses with available items. Create separate child `FulfillmentShipment` records for each allocated warehouse with their respective quantities. If total network-wide inventory is strictly less than requested, reject with `400 Bad Request` and make zero database modifications.

tasks.title: Race Condition Protection with Row-Level Locking
tasks.description:
When multiple customers order the same popular SKU simultaneously, uncoordinated reads and updates result in negative warehouse inventory counts.

**Goal:** Protect `WarehouseStock` rows using `select_for_update()` inside `transaction.atomic()` during fulfillment calculation and deduction. Add a Django database `CheckConstraint(condition=models.Q(quantity__gte=0), name='prevent_negative_stock')` to guarantee negative quantities are impossible at the database level.

tasks.title: Automated Reorder Trigger & Idempotent Restock Requests
tasks.description:
Warehouse managers do not receive timely alerts when stock drops below safety levels, causing replenishment delays.

**Goal:** Immediately following a successful stock deduction, check if `quantity <= reorder_threshold`. If the threshold is breached, automatically create a `PurchaseReorder` record with status `PENDING`. If a reorder record for that SKU and warehouse already exists in `PENDING` or `PROCESSING` status, skip creation to prevent duplicate procurement orders.
